# `•rand` — Generator

`•rand seed` returns a generator: a keyed vector of two functions that draw random numbers. The seed is a nonnegative whole number. The same seed gives the same draws.

- `roll Y` works like `¿Y`.
- `X deal Y` works like `X¿Y`.

A distribution's `sample` takes a generator on its left, as in `g d.sample 3`. Each draw takes the generator's next stream when it runs. A draw's numbers depend on the seed and on how many draws came before it, not on how many numbers those draws produced. Copies of a generator share its count.

A [map](../terms.qmd#term-map) draws for each cell separately, in cell order, whether or not it runs as a [batched call](../evaluation.qmd#functions-and-effects), so both give the same numbers. A guard that splits the cells is the exception: each side of the guard draws for its own cells in turn. A whole-array draw and a map of draws over the same items take different streams, so `¿v` and `¿¨v` give different numbers.

```bpl
g←•rand 3 ◇ h←•rand 3 ◇ (g.roll 4ρ6)≡h.roll 4ρ6    ⍝ $t
```

`¿` draws from the session's own generator, which [`•prefs ["seed":n]`](prefs.qmd) seeds.

Errors: `DOMAIN` for a seed that is not a nonnegative whole number, or a left argument to `sample` that is not a generator; `LENGTH` or `RANK` for more than one seed; `SYNTAX` for a dyadic call to `•rand`.
